DCP-LETT-1154.note: Sunday assigned February 6, 1848 from Ramsay/Owen invitations. Museum report Wednesday says Waterhouse expected back soon; return itself not established. DCP-LETT-1156.note: February 12, supplied 1848. Answers missing Williamson letter; lagoon mud cannot be found and only supposes all went to Ehrenberg. Ascension incrustation enclosed, Gold Coast/Devon specimens already seen, Australian shell series and gypsum sent or enclosed as described. DCP-LETT-1157.note: February14, supplied1848 from Admiralty commission. Requests Phillips reference and more cases/details of boulders above parent rock; current asserted true explanation remains Darwin hypothesis. Hopkins, Milne, Hitchcock and Glen Roy observations cited with own limited care. Heights and further observations queried, not later established numbers. Separate Admiralty suggestions sought. Printed1848paper in apparatus is later outcome, not missing Phillips answer or current final theory.

DCP-LETT-1158.note: Composite Hooker letter headed February 20, ending March 16. P1–11 report cheetah/hawk hunting and infertility, river limits, elephant varieties and behavior, dogs/cattle/color/altitude, climate after deforestation, spiders/swallow migrations, kunkar and salts, coal, barberry and Vallisneria. Many facts are informant reports or conjectures, not all personal observations. Crocodile disappearance after total deforestation is prospective, contrary to the synopsis implication of completed extinction. P6 crocodile postscript was inserted with March 4 blue-ink section. P12–17 March 4 cover itinerary, Calcutta patrons, quoted Thomson geology, heart symptoms and uncertain future travel; Thomson quotation stays attributed. P18–21 March 8 revise the route away from Calcutta. P22–25 literal February 16 is corrected to March 16 from itinerary: only this final section acknowledges a missing Darwin letter received through Falconer just before leaving Mirzapore. Griffith journals are recommended but Hooker has not studied them. Borneo plans are prospective. Separate Darwin pencil scores have no demonstrated contemporary annotation date. Earlier cheetah inquiry 889 is an ongoing documented question, not proved sole immediate prompt.

DCP-LETT-1158A.note: February 25, supplied 1848, date context inferred. And 30 Mar annotation probably records missing Ross answer, not Darwin receipt date. Later apparatus says Balanus resumed late 1850, conflicting with other contemporary progress stages; do not harmonize all sources into one definite schedule.

Darwin asks Higgins to fit them around rent collection, then adds the option of retaining £5 at Lady Day. The source summary incorrectly says February 15. DCP-LETT-1165.note: March 25, supplied 1848 from Mallet/Herschel connections. Answers missing Ball enquiry, cannot identify enclosed or described hook and offers limited remembered fishing/food observations. DCP-LETT-1166.note: Sunday assigned March 26, 1848. Offers unsolicited microscope advice, uncertain whether Owen instructions already submitted. Large fixed stage holding three-inch saucer is key advantage over old Beagle instrument; distinguishes Brown recommendation, Chevalier model and Smith/Beck manufacture. Offers fuller description, not proof enclosure already sent. Oral talk at Down is past, next London meeting prospective after illness. Silence to be interpreted as advice superfluous is a historical requested convention, not actual assent or an agent instruction. Later advertising, Lubbock ownership and manual editions are separate apparatus.

DCP-LETT-1166A.note: March 28, supplied 1848, Admiralty manuscript search. Missing Herschel message says parcel not received or mislaid, Darwin strongly believes Admiralty has it but no proof. His tentative March 15 posting belief conflicts with independently accepted March 21 enclosure letter and March 20 completion; preserve belief and correction separately. Full 50-page manuscript unavailable. Raw addressee R A B Hamilton versus identified W A B Hamilton remains explicit. Search asked, possible Auckland involvement conjecture; footnote March 23 Herschel instruction/stamp March 28 are not full incoming text or proved Darwin receipt. May registered resend is later.

DCP-LETT-1167.note: Saturday assigned April 1, 1848. Missing Henslow note offered London meeting but Darwin already arranged Monday; no accomplished encounter. Address received and read, including Whewell tides anecdote and practical-use claim explicitly criticized: truth-seeking described as intrinsic motive. Do not use later practical benefits of barnacle work to erase contemporary belief that it might remain unapplied. Pencil of the and quotation marks possibly Henslow additions in apparatus, not unqualified Darwin original. Recent separate-sex/minute male finding is provisional one-genus account, not all later classification. Hooker news reported and letters requested, not currently possessed on that basis. Sixth child prospective, microscope already made from Darwin model/Hooker hints. Quoted address passage is not a complete incoming Henslow letter.

DCP-LETT-1167F.note: Sunday assigned April 2, 1848 through fortnight since geology submission and planned London call, not a wholly independent exact date. Sends expanded microscope advice as separate notes, allows editorial cuts, credits actual Hooker dissection experience and Hooker/Brown lens recommendations. The geology manuscript believed lost at Admiralty is a different item, sent about fortnight earlier. Requests quarter-hour Wednesday talk and examination of Thompson book/Goadby preparations; planned inspection is not already-read evidence. Thanks Owen synopsis headings and hopes for print. Later published text, edition changes and probable Ibla topic remain editorial. No preserved incoming request or microscope enclosure text here.

DCP-LETT-1168.note: April 7, supplied 1848. Asks Ramsay to establish disputed Moel Tryfan height; Darwin cannot recall authority for own lower figure. Footnote compares Trimmer 1000, Darwin 1192, cited Murchison 1692, and later paper 1392 feet. None is an incoming answer or current resolved measurement. April 19 presentation is future; keep explicit uncertainty and unknown reply.

DCP-LETT-1169.note: April 7, supplied 1848. Incomplete damaged defence of coral theory follows De la Beche suggestion and published address, not a source-complete personal incoming letter. Palaeontographical publication proposal still under consideration and sequencing uncertain; later acceptance not backdated.

DCP-LETT-1297.note: January 25, supplied 1850. Fossil box arrived this morning, mostly uninjured except possibly Anatifera valves. Only a hasty first glance underlies species comparisons; P. medius/sulcatus classification is provisional. Forchhammer note enabled recovery from mineral dealer, who had failed to notify Darwin; exact incoming recovery note missing. Seeing Alepas does not establish complete dissection. Northern material still requested. Receipt, examination and final published taxonomy remain distinct.

DCP-LETT-1298.note: Monday evening assigned January 28, 1850 through neighboring letters. Latest Fitch lot arrived safely; one intermediate specimen confirms maximum and sulcatum as varieties rather than species, more valuable than a new species. Two new species from Morris arrived by same morning post, separate shipment. Five named forms listed with maximum varieties sulcatum/solidulum; four called new. Raw HTML splits list and includes diag/ramme artefacts, duplicate I numbering and S. Sowerby slip; preserve original versus editorial correction rather than silently normalizing. Productus later renamed angelini, not already that name here. Missing note conveys twenty years collecting and ill health. No preserved incoming letter or known exact receipt for every earlier lot.

DCP-LETT-1299.note: February 1 with supplied 1850 year. Reports five workdays lost to illness and 2½ hours worked on other days, confirmed MathML rather than 212. About 200 specimens, eleven described, at least twelve more expected; numbers are current progress, not final totals. Next Wednesday drawing visit planned, longer loan requested under silence convention and return labels promised. No proof silent permission or completed travel at this date.

DCP-LETT-1300.note: February3 with editorial1850 year: newspaper first brought imprisonment news, then Darwin wrote Henslow and received a note from Sir William through that route. This is distinct from any direct incoming J.D.Hooker prompt. Liberation is hoped to occur before letter arrival, not known; continuing collecting and return home are conditional. Health plateau, cold baths, no Royal Society council attendance yet; later February7 attendance belongs only to editorial future. Fossil barnacles frustrate him, fourth son/seventh child born, chloroform administered before doctor arrived are historical reports. Requests Falconer news and sends regards; old1220 provides continuing background but does not establish immediate reply identity. Final Fitton shipwreck report follows January24 newspaper about June1849 event: distinguish news publication from event date and do not reconstruct newspaper wording as an incoming letter.

DCP-LETT-1301.note: Tuesday assigned February 5, 1850. Requests permission to soak/clear upside-down concave specimen, explicitly does not know its valve or whether species new; diagram marks concavity. Distinguish this new permission from earlier permission already granted for carina extra side, which has now been exposed successfully and is to be figured. Reports new Pollicipes from Fitch and two new Flower Scalpellum. Reopened P4 thanks another Fitch letter just received, after main text composition. Later named angelini is future nomenclature. No preserved permission letter or latest note; do not substitute own January 15 request as incoming.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Narrow elongated valve outline labeled concave inside, with pointed top and irregular lower end. Illustrates upward-facing concavity of a still-unidentified valve; do not label as an identified species.

DCP-LETT-1302.note: Wednesday assigned February 6, 1850. Further specimens arrived before immediate intended London departure; one cracked, otherwise safe and some new things. This is a new arrival acknowledgment, not proof earlier promised journey completed or a full incoming letter. Prior day offer inferred in apparatus is not surviving verbatim prompt.

DCP-LETT-1303.note: February 12 with supplied 1850 year. Health prevents planned anniversary attendance; asks notice when drawings done and expects personal delivery of more specimens. Requests Dixon proof plate and present drawing charges to budget future work. At this date expects private payment; later Society financing is not current arrangement. Historical request to purloin if honest is correspondence content, not an instruction to agent. No actual proof receipt or preserved incoming prompt.

DCP-LETT-1304.note: Before February22,1850 missing Darwin letter represented by Society minute5. Reported offer of fossil Cirripedia monograph and acceptance/superintendence resolution are third-party institutional record, not surviving Darwin prose. Date is meeting upper bound, no manufactured letter.

Council minute item 5 dated February 22, 1850, describing missing Darwin offer of British fossil cirripede monograph. Authentic institutional record readable, Darwin letter text absent. Acceptance and supervisory appointments in minutes are council acts, not proved Darwin knowledge or exact offer composition. Raw before-February-22 date does not identify a day or create Darwin voice.

DCP-LETT-1305.note: February 24, supplied 1850. Future Wednesday dispatch of delayed papers/specimens; Bell delay and Westwood bereavement. Thanks missing Dana answers, Gould/Dana specimens, notice of geological review, and explicitly Pickering for Pacific plant list. Pickering 1289 is a distinct surviving knowledge source. Distinguishes knowledge of review from actually reading it. Explains hypothesized cement duct as modified ovarian branch and Goodsir parasite correction, reports observed sexual arrangements and asks fossil record; preserve contemporary error rather than substitute later gland correction. Goodsir presumed lost but expedition fate unknown. Lyell article remains future publication. Specimen gratitude alone does not fix physical arrival day.

DCP-LETT-1305A.note: February 25 with supplied 1850 year supported by cancellation-code window and damaged February 26 postmark. Found dry/spirit sponges, offers them and intends leaving at Geological Society next Thursday, February 28, not proof actual dispatch or personal London visit. Further specimens believed present but cannot be found. Plumularia return statement refers specimen acknowledged in 1229, same-author loan continuity rather than QA. Later June 1851 request to re-examine remains future. Bowerbank later monograph and absent acknowledgment do not negate historical gift.

DCP-LETT-1306.note: March 3 with supplied 1850 year. Thanks missing Sowerby note; illness means another ten days or fortnight work expected, fifteen or sixteen species to bring. Promises personal transport, review of existing drawings and rough sketches. Society has now agreed fossil publication; asks whether Sowerby wants engraving commission. Dixon proof still requested; Loricula to be engraved and borrowed specimens to be locked up. Distinguish current estimate from final 45 species in future plates; no completed delivery, proof receipt or fully engraved volume.

DCP-LETT-1306F.note: March 3, supplied1850. First approach to Dunker follows missing Morris advice; Copenhagen loan already includes specified fossils and drawings known. Requests Roemer species/unknown material, future careful return. Does not prove Roemer specimens already received or a direct incoming Dunker reply. Species names preserved at contemporary stage.

DCP-LETT-1307.note: March 4, 1850 surviving copy. Woodd manuscript read with attention, but unlocated and apparently unpublished. Darwin expresses lack of mathematical mechanics, questions bowing versus crumpling, pressure transmission through viscid rock, heat-wave migration and sediment loading. Tentative criticism is not established mechanism or complete rejection of every heat effect. Encourages real sections and constrained speculation. Diagrams praised in missing manuscript are not preserved images. Editorial later and comparative sources remain separate.

DCP-LETT-1308.note: Friday assigned March 8, 1850. Received and read Lyell presidential address sooner than expected; February 15 delivery does not date Darwin reading. Praises Murchison criticism and clock metaphor, anticipates future organic hour-hand address. Missing private account of anniversary dinner supplies Mahon compliment and Bunsen speech; Darwin recalls a separate 1836 Herschel conversation. Health deterioration restricts London travel and barnacle work progresses slowly. Raises a new Scania/Denmark Lower Cretaceous query from specimen labels and von Buch, requesting optional answer by Lady Lyell. No preserved incoming text supplies those missing private communications.

DCP-LETT-1309.note: March8,1850 Scarborough. Reports evergreen phlox from annual Drummondii crossed with perennial forms despite latter dying back; promises further experiments and carefully disclaims priority for hybrid plant itself, claiming only possibly novel observation. Rhododendron/azalea analogy ends without closing punctuation in surviving text. Darwin double scoring and portfolio17 annotation show later use/filing but are undated. No current dated Darwin witness; proposed continuation of1278 remains candidate only, not an automatically identified reverse reply.

DCP-LETT-1310.note: Friday evening conjectured March 8, 1850 from March 17 follow-up; apparatus excludes March 15 only as probably insufficient time for response, not logically impossible. Exact-date hold retained. Misdirected missing letter travelled via Farnham and arrived yesterday; do not turn relative day into securely March 7. Loan specimen includes presumed new Chthamalus and B. cranchii; later taxonomy remains separate. Offers purchase or retention as loan, payment completed only by later 1312 stamps. Society acceptance now heard, drawings/MS still being prepared. Copper engraving required for growth lines; Sowerby drawing already under way but engraving preference not completed commission. Hanley address still requested; membership only supposed, not proved admission.

DCP-LETT-1311.note: Saturday assigned January 26–March 1850 after Copenhagen receipt and before next Hancock letter. Footnote upper rationale depends on 1316, itself March 31 OR April 7; if April 7, Saturday April 6 is not excluded by that rationale though outside encoded March range. Preserve conflict rather than silently extend. Molluscs now bottled with roughly sixty packets and old colour/location notes; next Wednesday dispatch intended, specimens gifted permanently but manuscript to be preserved. Clitia specimens force retreat from earlier Alcippe/Arthrobalanus explanation; retain literal give-up wording without turning uncertainty into a categorical no-burrowing assertion. Still defends mechanical Lithotrya apparatus, seeks confirmation of marginal corrosion and chemical solution. Answers missing Goodsir-male question, reporting two genuinely separate parasitic males as own finding. Alcippe and newly obtained Alepas remain unexamined. Do not substitute later surviving copies of Beagle notes for missing sent originals.

DCP-LETT-1312.note: March 17 with supplied 1850 year independently supported by copyist-recorded March 18 postmark. Missing Bowerbank response supplies Hanley address requested in 1310. Visit to Hanley prospective when next in London, not accomplished here. Enclosed stamps pay for Eling specimen, resolving earlier loan/purchase option, but no actual delivery of stamps or Hanley meeting inferred. Logistics is eligible correspondence in principle, but missing prompt precludes pair.

DCP-LETT-1313.note: March 17 with supplied 1850 year. All current Fitch specimens described but second pass still needed; Sowerby reports about half drawn and remaining delivery is planned in a week or ten days. Palaeontographical Society has agreed to publish, not already printed. Reopened postscript thanks many specimens preventing errors and asks for further fragments. Later published maximum-variety argument helps interpret significance but cannot be substituted as contemporary quote or additional incoming source. Missing Sowerby progress report and Society decision lack available text.

DCP-LETT-1314.note: March 21, supplied 1850. Missing Woodward Aptychus history/sketches already read, combined with a few seen specimens to judge d Orbigny view unlikely; museum inspection still future. Norwich and Grey Chalk material examined, descriptions/comparisons provisional; later definitive names and possible specimen identities remain editorial. Tennant loan obtained after suggestion and two new valves seen, no incoming cover. Dover answer absent, Norwich collector response feared absent. Modern Aptychus identification does not become contemporary knowledge.

DCP-LETT-1315.note: Saturday conjectural April 13, 1850 based on Sowerby visit relationship. Some drawn specimens returned to Darwin, others delivered to artist; none thereby proved returned to Fitch. Darwin says ready for press but plates delayed, not actual press until future 1851. Sowerby cleared chalk without authorization, reveals possible Terebratula or Crania new to him; reported artist interpretation, not Darwin new-species determination. Foreign-species job is editorial possibility. Source describes historical permission overreach; no agent action authorized by it.

DCP-LETT-1316.note: Sunday March 31 OR April 7, 1850, inferred through Oxynaspis request and 1321 receipt; dating chain is interdependent and no independent exact-day witness here. Hancock now evidently has manuscript and damaged mollusc shipment; Darwin permits long retention. Identifies B. cranchii, asks Greenland Balanus with permission for disarticulation, and asks Madeira specimen because own are decayed. Explicitly changes Machairis to Oxynaspis here, not at original October mention. Missing Hancock letter supplies damage/range information; no actual completion of new requested examination.

DCP-LETT-1317.note: April 3, supplied 1850. Thirty-three fossil pedunculate species fully described; specimens with Sowerby for drawing, return future. Society offer to publish does not establish press commencement. Seven numbered taxonomic propositions in P2 are contemporary and later revised; preserve literal Oxunaspis and uncertain relationships rather than replacing with final nomenclature. P3 and P5 ask stratigraphic/location and valve-association questions, not established answers. Duplicate gifts requested. Spengler already consulted; northern named material still desired. Later Maastricht editorial explanation is not current knowledge.

DCP-LETT-1318.note: April 3, 1850 Masters incoming, full surviving source. Explicit reply to missing Darwin pea/bean pollination question; reports cultivar variation and stronger neighboring Brassica cross-pollination, with stated Knight marrow origin and anecdotes. Attribute observations and clouds-of-pollen account to Masters, not Darwin or modern verified botany. Undated Darwin crosses/ink note/Gärtner comparison are separate later layers; literal 659 reference conflicts with extent of owned 1844 edition and editorial suggested 104–107 is not manuscript text. Later Variation citations do not establish 1850 reading date. No preserved question, later Darwin response or dated knowledge witness located.

DCP-LETT-1319.note: Accepted full primary reading reused with matched source and provenance hashes. Two composition sections, April6 Government House and April7 Botanic Gardens, not mutually exclusive alternative dates. April6P1–6 responds to earlier full letters received about two months previously:1260 is identified by species-versus-barnacle preference and correction of Yangma dam to moraine. Hooker says theories interest but do not convert him, reports well-marked Sikkim willows/Rubi/Senecios/Gnaphalia despite equable climate and revises Himalayan drainage, snowline and glacier model. Falconer/Thomson and Humboldt views are attributed, current theory provisional. April7P8 recounts five-month parcel withholding, seven Frances letters released, reconciliation and good health; only later within this section explicitly acknowledges February letter received this morning and responds to incomplete cure and seven children, identifying1300. Do not let this April7 input condition April6 prose. Nepal permission attempt fails, Sylhet/Khassya/Manipur journey and Thomson joining prospective; later May1 departure is editorial. DCP-LETT-1319F.note: April 7, 1850 endorsed. Missing Salt sympathy/assistance and offer of safe three-to-three-and-a-half-thousand-pound investment accepted on trust without party names. Will write today to Robarts for six-thousand-five-hundred-pound Exchequer Bills; intention not proven purchase. Later April 17 Corbett investment is a distinct editorial event. Possible relation to brother cash only conjectural, no incoming bank instruction recovered.

DCP-LETT-1320.note: April 8, supplied 1850 from scientific/itinerary context. Found delayed Gould parcel yesterday at Cuming, where servant had put it aside during illness; earlier delivery there differs from Darwin access. Coronula promised by missing note was not enclosed; only large Balanus present. Dana hope of Scalpellum holdings reported, no incoming Dana text. Previous Darwin reminder missing. Yesterday would be April 7 under assigned year; April 10 meeting cited in apparatus is contextual, not identical visit day established.

DCP-LETT-1321.note: Day 15 with supplied April 1850, editorially linked to 1316 request. New specimens safely arrived by this delayed acknowledgment; Madeira one deliberately held until return to Pedunculata work, not already dissected. Balanus identified with little/no opening, return promised, earlier mixed specimens recalled. Greenland latitude requested, Iceland occurrence already known. Still convinced all Lithotrya bore but mechanism uncertain. Later Balanus priority name in apparatus does not replace current names. No exact specimen arrival day or surviving incoming cover.

DCP-LETT-1322.note: April 28 with supplied 1850 year. Recent missing Sulivan letter from Falklands asks vessel, November expedition and six-week route via Gallegos/St Julian/Bahia Blanca, without salary; fallback £150–200 charter unaffordable. Darwin asks Owen to prompt Beaufort, plans to reply, expects society help unlikely. This current logistical request is not preserved 1845 fossil-discovery letter 730. Thanks prior missing Owen introduction to Mrs Dixon but declines Worthing journey; renews exact plate XXVIII figure 9 Xiphidium request from 1357. Prospectus already sent; hoped lectures publication never completed according to later apparatus. No acquired specimen or successful expedition inferred.

DCP-LETT-1323.note: Thursday in May 1850, not an independently chosen exact day. Responds to missing Fox caution about harmful water-cure cases; regularly reports to Gully and changes treatment, does not endorse treating himself without guidance. Wants Fox doctor opinion while acknowledging individual uncertainty. Recently improved after six-week retrograde period, qualifying earlier absolute cure language. Chloroform comments attributed to Simpson/own contemporary opinion; do not convert to clinical truth. Egerton farm praise came orally weeks earlier, not from a preserved incoming Fox letter. Gully visit desired but travelling resisted; no accomplished trip implied.

DCP-LETT-1324.note: May 4 with supplied 1850 year. Society has just limited foreign illustrations to one plate equivalent; asks hold on four named species pending packing and exact progress report. April 26 committee decision in apparatus dates institutional event, not Darwin receipt. Later inclusion of all named species is not current authorization or completed layout. No preserved incoming Council instruction or Sowerby answer.

DCP-LETT-1325.note: May 5 with supplied 1850 year. Two more specimens safely received, valves new to Fitch collection but unsuitable as basis for specific names. New-to-collection does not mean new species. No incoming cover text preserved and no precise arrival time beyond acknowledgment.

DCP-LETT-1326.note: May 9, supplied 1850. Accepts Higgins proposal of a 15 percent reduction for the past half-year, hopes depressed times temporary and compares prices under protection and in France. Asks whether Hardy works actively and has any complaint. Specific proposal is missing; 1279 is Darwin own earlier concern, not an incoming prompt. Editorial continuation of reduced income through 1852 is future knowledge.

DCP-LETT-1327.note: May 12 with supplied 1850 year. Explicitly only just read Hancock 1848 mollusc-boring paper because periodicals not read promptly; publication and ownership do not establish earlier knowledge. Sends one of three Lithotrya specimens after moult, distinguishes moulting scales from valves; lacks basal cup specimen though previously borrowed examples. Remains undecided between entering and enlarging existing hole or initial larval boring; planned Clisia examination future. Missing Hancock request for more information/specimens is reported, not preserved. Published 1851/1854 conclusions remain later.

DCP-LETT-1328.note: May20, supplied1850. Explicitly thanks missing April27 geological letter for full clear answers. Steenstrup specimens have been used,33 fossil pedunculates described and now with Sowerby for drawings; no exact delivery date. Prior1270 specimen dispatch is background, not the April27 information. Editorial possibility that information answers Darwin April3 Steenstrup query is routing context, not a preserved incoming substitute.

DCP-LETT-1329.note: May 20, supplied 1850. Circular just received, quotes free-journal offer and requests missing numbers since last 1845 volume to Athenaeum. Quoted sentence does not recover whole circular, request does not prove delivery/read. Last received volume year is not exact last delivery date. Secretary identity not named.

DCP-LETT-1330.note: May 20, supplied 1850; freshly fully reread here after batch-17 extra reading. Missing last Steenstrup letter answered all long questions, but actual answers not reproduced. Sowerby drawing delayed and northern specimens awaited. Lithotrya drawing already known, boring method new; later December forwarding is not first knowledge. Hermaphroditism work heard of but not seen; Danish unreadable and German difficult, later Busk translation distinct. Preserve original hermaphroditism wording and keep editorial self-fertilisation explanation separate. Injury/impregnation observation and two parasitic-male cases are contemporary reports.

Additional full reading of May 20 with supplied 1850 year, Darwin to Steenstrup. Missing reply answers questions, drawings of loan specimens delayed, northern material still anticipated. Specifically thanks Lithotrya drawing and says indicated boring manner new to him: establishes drawing known by May 20, not first seen December 25. Hermaphroditism work heard of but unseen, Danish unreadable and German difficult; later November reading/translation remain later. Keep literal improbable hermaphroditism wording distinct from editor explanation about self-fertilization. Injured Balanus and parasitic males are contemporary observations. This is another outgoing witness, not preserved incoming drawing text or a direct pair.

DCP-LETT-1331.note: May 22, supplied 1850. Forwards Joseph Hooker letter to William, then requests onward Henslow circulation. Specific geological motto and complimentary book discussion identify 1257 independently of generic Dear Darwin salutation; apparatus explicitly confirms September 30 letter. Darwin already read it by May 22, improving previously recorded June 13 witness from 1339. This is cross-correspondent knowledge/routing, not a direct answer to Joseph. Actual initial arrival remains unknown; surviving 1257 is incomplete and later Darwin annotations undated.

DCP-LETT-1333.note: Sunday assigned May 26, 1850 by proposed June 3/4 visit and time for reply; June 2 considered too late by editors, not exact date independently proven. Urges progress, proposes direct copper drawing and rough outlines for arranging plates. Manuscript ready but illustrations unfinished; Council pressure is reported. Future June 5 presentation and account-book expense are dating evidence, not prior completed visit or preserved incoming prompt.

DCP-LETT-1334.note: May 27, supplied 1850. Explicitly received Higgins letter and account this morning; separately advised by bankers of £183 5s 11d draft. Glad of good account of Hardy farming. These are two distinct communications; neither text survives. Exact morning receipt is supported for missing Higgins note, not for 1161 or all prior financial news.

DCP-LETT-1335.note: Monday 27 assigned August 1849 by narrow mourning border and calendar, with alternatives November 1848 and May 1850 discussed and rejected editorially. Declines missing Ransome invitation because health requires regularity, has written Maguire. Summary claims December 1850 Henslow inauguration, inconsistent with assigned date and footnote suggesting portrait-publication dinner in 1849. Preserve unresolved event identity; later portrait sitting not current attendance. No Ransome input survives.

DCP-LETT-1336.note: Saturday assigned April 13, 1850 through London visit and likely garden weather, not an independently certain day; February visit is an alternative considered unlikely, and relation to June 8 provides upper context. Yesterday reviewed drawings: outlines mostly good but wants harder growth lines, less shading, rigid accuracy over artistic effect. P4 reveals some quadratum valves incorrect and inside scuta indistinct, stronger critique than initial trifling changes. Thursday garden walk did not occur. Actual drawings are inputs but not preserved here; printed Mineral conchology comparison and future corrected plates are distinct.

DCP-LETT-1337.note: Saturday assigned June 8, 1850. Own ripple observations 6–10 feet below low water are distinct from Siau report of 60–70 feet. Width-depth relationship is a conjecture he cannot yet establish. Parker work found at brother house has uncertain bibliographic identity. Emma thanks Lady Lyell for missing news note; Darwin thanks Lyell for approval of his paper. P4 first sentence about Agassiz Lake Superior book is Darwin, followed within the same paragraph by editorial heading From Emma Darwin to M. E. Lyell. P5–6 are Emma, including tickets, hippopotamus, future Tuesday Malvern trip and Katharine pregnancy. Character-level split required. Book received by this letter, but subsequent August reading witness must not be backdated. Later journey and October birth remain future apparatus.

DCP-LETT-1338.note: Autograph Saturday June 9 corrected editorially to June 8, 1850 because June 8 is Saturday and planned Malvern June 11–18 fits. Keep literal and correction separately. Pleased with harder drawings after prior criticism, sends written notes and specimens for corrections; two figures need substantial attention. Extra natural-size glaber figure desired, laevis figures uncertain and identity later ambiguous. Allows completed extra drawings but forbids further foreign additions, limits English extras. Offers payment and requests rough arranged plates; future June 28 Council scheme submission not already accomplished. Accompanying drawings and notes absent.

DCP-LETT-1339.note: June13 with supplied1850 year, written Malvern while source letters locked atDown. Last letter received about fortnight ago gives approximate late-May event, not exactMay30. This answer combines1257 and1319: P2 poem, cold-finger SouthAmerica reading, inverted strata and P6 Malcolmson correction match1257; glacier continuity and transverse rivers also engage1319. P3 philosophical-mind reassurance answers1319P4 self-deprecation.
